As soon as you walk into the office, dust and allergens are in the air due to a weak HVAC system. The space only has one restroom which is located in the back part of the office.

versions.request: Improve public housing maintenance and cleanliness
versions.explanation: The poor upkeep of the William Ried Houses is well known. Requests for repairs are usually met with rebuke by the local managing agent. Soot left by a fire last year lingered on the wall for weeks until the intervention of NYS Senator Zellnor Y. Myrie. NYCHA needs to increase funding to complete repairs and increase monitoring to insure that repairs tickets are not simply closed out.
versions.response: OMB supports the agency's position as follows: Agency supports but cannot accommodate Explanation: The Quality & Cost Control (QCC) Department—formerly known as the Quality Assurance Department—was established to oversee the quality of repairs and performance across NYCHA’s Section 9 portfolio. Its primary goal is to ensure that work completed in both public areas and individual apartments meets internal benchmarks and industry standards. The department carries out a range of recurring inspections, along with investigative and administrative reviews, to identify and address substandard work, prevent misconduct, and resolve complaints efficiently. QA inspectors perform visual inspections of a random sample of closed Corrective Maintenance WO (“CM WOs”) tickets during their ongoing rotation of development visits throughout the year. The inspections are performed on CM WOs that were completed by maintenance and skilled trades workers within the past 15 days of QCC’s visit to the development to ensure that recent repairs were completed up to industry standards. Unsatisfactory work result in the automatic creation of follow up work orders for the development in Maximo. In Q2 - 2025, QCC began to utilize the QA Dashboard to optimize selection of NYCHA locations and crafts to focus on for QCC follow-up. The dashboard is functioning as intended, and the Quality Assurance Unit is working with the Federal Monitor to continue improving the dashboard through small modifications, as needed, such as the ability to search corrective maintenance work tickets using specific date ranges versus just a month as originally designed. Residents who have concerns about specific conditions in their apartments or public areas that were supposed to be addressed can submit a complaint form through the NYCHA website (see link below, under "Submit a Concern"). Upon receiving the complaint, the Quality & Cost Control (QCC) Department will conduct a follow-up inspection. There will be no retaliation or disciplinary action taken against anyone who reports an issue, concern, or violation in good faith. This includes reporting attempts to conceal problems—such as covering holes with cardboard or wood or shutting off water to hide leaks
